question.text: From which picture did Jiang Wanqing conclude that emotional companionship ranks first? Please provide the session number and the picture file name.

supporting_evidence.content: Haha, I recently came across a survey on the main reasons young people keep pets, and I thought I'd share it with you. It reminded me of when you shared a photo of a trophy before we played badminton, saying that sports are a way to relax. Now, it seems that keeping pets has become a more everyday form of "emotional decompression" and a "lifestyle choice," even replacing some social needs.

Emotional companionship ranks first, which aligns with consumer psychology. Just as you emphasized the value of community when analyzing fitness apps, pets can also fulfill social needs—albeit in the form of a more stable and controllable "emotional community." This reminds me of what you mentioned earlier when reviewing protein powder: brands enhance loyalty through community engagement. In the pet economy, the logic of "pet owner communities" might be even more fundamental and enduring.

questions.validation_notes: It is inferred that the image (3.png) drives the text to focus on causal inference, which aligns with the image-driven text requirement of Multimodal (Text-Image) Causal Inference.
